newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Few Brazil 1995/96 crop soybeans left for export.
newsitem.headline: Few Brazil 1995/96 crop soybeans left for export.

text.p: Brazil will no longer be able to compete on the international spot soybean market until the start of 1996/97 harvest around February after producers have sold almost all of the 1995/96 crop, traders said.

"Soybean product availability is zero at producer level," said Tony Fagundes, vice president of Mato Grosso state-based cooperative Cooperlucas. "The little that remains will go to the domestic market."
Two leading traders said around 90 percent of Brazil's 1995/96 crop of an estimated 23.2 million tonnes has now been sold, and that available stocks are considered low.
Independent analyst Safras e Mercado meanwhile put current availability of 1995/96 soybeans still to be sold at less than 1.5 million tonnes.
"This is less than normal at this time of year," said Safras' analyst Flavio Franca. "What's available will go to the domestic market".
However, there is still a little soymeal and some soyoil available for export," Franca said.
